thread:
kevin (Eng): Quick question  I'm UK-based and have 2.5 days of PTO left but we have a year-end shutdown 12/24-12/27. Can I carry 1 day over or swap to a floating day for Dec 23?

paula (Manager): i can approve a swap if policy allows. can people-ops confirm cutoff + whether part-days are allowed?

ana (People Ops): policy refresher: standard carryover requires a formal request by 12/10 and is approved sparingly. floating day conversion is possible for local statutory observances when they conflict with shutdown but we need manager approval + payroll notified before cutoff.

kevin (Eng): the complication is i'm on parental leave earlier this year and my accruals were prorated. does that affect eligibility?

ana (People Ops): parental leave proration doesn't disqualify you, but accrual/proration can change the numeric balance. we can do a one-day exception for prorated balances; file via HR portal -> Time Off Exceptions and mark "parential leave proration" in notes. deadline for exceptions to affect year-end balances is 12/15.

mike (Payroll): technical note: if the exception is submitted after 12/15 it will still be honored for pay but will show on next year's reconciliation. also part-day swaps (e.g., 0.5 day) are allowed but must be entered as hours in WorkDay and match manager approval screenshot.

paula (Manager): i approve the swap to Dec 23 (half-day AM). kevin, please submit the exception and attach my approval screenshot.

timebot: reminder scheduled for 12/10: submit time-off exceptions for year-end adjustments.

kevin (Eng): submitted the form and attached screenshot 11/29. form ID #TOE-2026-721.

nana (People Ops): received. i'll escalate to payroll and add a People Ops note. quick FYI: contractors and vendors don't get floating conversions; full/part-time employees can request.

mike (Payroll): logged the adjustment. will confirm once processed in WorkDay; expect change visible on final December statement if processed by 12/15.

kevin (Eng): sounds good, thanks all.

ana (People Ops): resolving thread. if anyone else in UK has similar conflicts with shutdown vs local observance, please group them so we can handle as a batch exception.
